result:
I found 12 rules whose behaviour didn't match their docstrings and fixed them all in `pricebook.py`. To find them, I wrote a script that turns each docstring into a reference calculation and compares it with the real function for quantities 0–299 across several unit prices. It flagged exactly these 12 rules, and after the fixes it reports no mismatches.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 04, 07, 58 | The cap only applied once the discount passed a higher threshold | Always cap the discount |
| 15 | Discount started at 21 units instead of 20 | Start at 20 (`>= 20`) |
| 41 | Discount started at 13 units instead of 12 | Start at 12 (`>= 12`) |
| 66 | Used `> 12`, so exactly 12 units got no discount | Changed to `>= 12` |
| 16, 117 | The cap was applied to the amount before the percentage, not to the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap it |
| 21 | Marked marginal but discounted every unit | Discount only units above 12 |
| 59, 72 | Used `round()`, but discounts should round down to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 136 | Took 6% instead of 5% | Changed to 5% |

STATUS: DONE
